primary_mathematical_proof: The sum of all four separate ribbon perimeters is unchanged. Joining removes both copies of each contact length: P_union=P_separate-2*S. Contact sums are first35+60+85=180, second60+60+35=155. Therefore P_second-P_first=2*(180-155)=50cm, B. Counting each contact only once gives25cm, C, the frozen wrong hypothesis. Source heights, overlaps, interfaces, all outer edges and four ribbons stay fixed.

formal_record.question:
Four ribbons each have width $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. Each ribbon is $25 \mathrm{~cm}$ longer than the next smallest ribbon. The ribbons are then arranged to form two different shapes as shown in the diagram. How much longer is the perimeter of the second shape than the perimeter of the first shape?
Choices:
A:$75 \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$50 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$25 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$20 \mathrm{~cm}$
E:$0 \mathrm{~cm}$
